News.title: New farming minister faints ‘at sight of meat’ after ‘feeling unwell’ while touring cold storage unit
News.content:
THE new farming minister fainted while visiting a refrigerated storage unit full of beef, it has been revealed.

Stephen Morgan has been on a tour of farms and suppliers since being appointed.



But he felt ill when stepping into the room filled with shelves of meat from slaughtered cattle at a food processing plant in the Lake District.

One local farmer, who knew about the incident, said: “He’d been shown large chunks of beef as well as some steaks but then he felt faint.



“He said something like, ‘I don’t feel too well — I need a moment.’”

He added: “It’s not a great look for the farming minister to faint at the sight of meat.”



The Portsmouth South MP explained of his wobble: “I felt unwell moving between the extreme heat and cold storage, and I’m grateful to all the staff at Lake District Farmers.

“Hats off to the brilliant ­people working in these conditions and temperatures to keep the nation fed.”

Prime Minister Andy Burnham is on a bid to “build back trust” with farmers after his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer faced protests over inheritance tax laws.

He has announced a £65million funding package for them, amid fears hot, dry weather could drive up food prices on supermarket shelves.



The National Farmers’ Union welcomed the measures but added that “it doesn’t affect the crisis today”.

News.title: Deer shot dead in Richmond Park after injuring man in his 60s on picnic as beast ‘looked for food’
News.content:
DEERY ME Deer shot dead in Richmond Park after injuring man in his 60s on picnic as beast ‘looked for food’

A DEER has been shot dead at a popular park in London after injuring a man in his 60s while he was having a picnic.

Emergency services rushed to Richmond Park on Saturday afternoon after an elderly man was attacked by a deer that was reportedly looking for food.



Police and ambulance staff raced to the scene and found a man in his 60s with chest injuries.

He was taken to hospital where the wounds were assessed as neither life-changing nor life threatening.



Due to the deer‘s behaviour, it was deemed dangerous to other visitors and the decision was made to put the animal down.

Richmond Park is popular with joggers and cyclists and is home to 600-strong herds of red and fallow deer.

The deer have roamed the park, which spans some 2,500 acres, since 1637.

Royal Parks have reiterated the importance of not approaching the deer and to not attempt to feed them.

A spokesperson said: “We understand from the police that thankfully the injuries were not life-threatening.

“Sadly, the stag’s behaviour meant that it had to be put down as it was deemed to be a danger to visitors.



“We suspect that this particular stag may have learnt to associate visitors with food.

“If visitors follow our advice and do not feed or interfere with the deer, it is highly unlikely that they will exhibit this type of behaviour.”

This comes after videos and photographs circulated online of park visitors approaching the deer and feeding them.

In one video, parents let a young children stroke one of the wild deer despite repeated safety warnings.

The alarming footage shows mums and dads encouraging youngsters to pet the deer on the head while others feed the herd.



Recently, Royal Parks said it was “shocked and alarmed” by similar behaviour of visitors in nearby Bushy Park and warned that this can prove dangerous as the animals can be unpredictable.

The spokesperson said: “This is highly dangerous behaviour.

“Deer in Bushy and Richmond Parks are wild animals and should never be fed, approached or touched.

“Repeated feeding can cause deer to lose their natural wariness of people and seek out food from visitors, creating risks for both people and wildlife.

“Getting this close, and offering food, puts people at real risk of serious injury.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

They added: “Our advice is simple. Keep at least 50 metres away, never feed or touch the deer, and if one comes towards you, put all food and packaging out of sight and move away slowly and calmly.

“Do not try to move the deer away yourself.”

News.title: Moment cops ram balaclava-clad underage driver, 15, in 67mph chase after driving at police – before knife found in boot
News.content:
THIS is the moment cops rammed into a balaclava-clad underage driver during a dangerous 67mph chase before finding a knife in the boot.

A boy, 15, driving a Land Rover Discovery in Adwick, Doncaster was arrested earlier this month on suspicion of dangerous driving, failing to stop and driving without insurance or a licence.



Dramatic footage released by South Yorkshire Police shows the Land Rover racing down a road as an officer drives after him.

The boy behind the wheel aggressively weaved through traffic, having previously hurtled head-on at police.



Cops responded to reports of the vehicle driving “erratically” and reaching speeds of 67mph in a 40mph zone, putting members of the public in danger.

The officer pursuing the boy speeds up to become parallel with the vehicle and makes a split-second decision to avert disaster.

He rams into the side of the car to force it to stop, and the Land Rover hits the kerb.

The car slows down and the occupants, wearing black balaclavas, are jolted to one side by the force of the collision.



Another officer who had been supporting the tactical stop on a motorbike pulls up in front of the Land Rover to block the front of the car.

Both cops run over to the vehicle and detain the driver.

The 15-year-old has since been bailed pending further enquiries.



Motorcycle and Rural Crime Team Sergeant James Shirley said: “Our officers worked as a team to quickly and professionally bring this pursuit to a safe conclusion and to prevent any harm coming to members of the public.

“The manner in which this vehicle was being driven posed a clear and immediate risk to the public, and the consequences could have been far more serious.

“Thankfully on this occasion no one was injured, but next time this could have been a different story.

“When someone chooses to drive recklessly, especially at high speeds and without the legal requirements of a licence or insurance, they endanger not only themselves but every pedestrian and road user around them.

“Dangerous drivers are not welcome on South Yorkshire’s roads, and while you can’t be responsible for everyone else’s actions, you can your own.



“Don’t put yourself, other road users and pedestrians in danger with your own reckless actions.

“Take responsibility and do you part to keep our roads safe as the implications could be life-changing.”

A spokesperson for South Yorkshire Police said: “A speeding vehicle being driven dangerously through the streets of Doncaster by a suspected underage driver was safely stopped after being pursued by officers from our Motorcycle and Rural Crime Team (MARCT).

“Earlier this month, officers from MARCT and our Roads Policing Group were carrying out an operation to combat vehicle-enabled crime when they were alerted to a Land Rover Discovery being driven erratically in the Adwick area, with its occupants seen wearing balaclavas.

“After it refused to stop for our MARCT officers, they engaged in a pursuit.



“With the vehicle continuing to pose a significant risk to the public, officers in a car made tactical contact to safely bring the Land Rover to a stop.

“Tactical contact is only used when deemed necessary to prevent serious harm, and in this case it allowed officers to end the pursuit in a controlled manner.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“A 15-year-old boy was arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving, failing to stop and driving without insurance or a licence.

“He was also arrested on suspicion of possession of an offensive weapon after a bladed article was found in the boot of the Land Rover during a thorough search of the vehicle.”

News.title: Mystery as cops quiz man who ripped down charity posters honouring tragic teen, 17, ‘stabbed to death by her ex at home’
News.content:
POSTER PROBE Mystery as cops quiz man who ripped down charity posters honouring tragic teen, 17, ‘stabbed to death by her ex at home’

A MAN has been caught on camera tearing down posters in memory of a 17-year-old teenager with the “biggest heart” who was stabbed to death.

CCTV footage shows him destroying fundraising flyers on lampposts with a picture of Lainie Williams, who died from multiple stab wounds after an attack in her home in South Wales.



Police questioned the man after the incident in the village of Cefn Fforest, near Blackwood.

No arrests have been made, but residents blasted the “horrible man” for dishonouring the efforts to pay tribute to the beloved teenager.



One woman, who lives in Cefn Fforest, said: “What’s wrong with this man what’s his issue with them being up.”

“Officers have spoken to a man following reports of criminal damage; no arrests were made,” a Gwent Police spokesperson said.



Neighbour Stephen Darknell, 48, is set to launch a 100-day challenge to run 5k every day in Lainie’s honour.

The money will go to the Wales Air Ambulance who were called to the tragic scene of the stabbing in November last year.

Stephen will kick off the challenge on August 21, which would have been the teenager’s 18th birthday.

“I live where Lainie lived, and I know the family and her grandparents, so I just thought I’d do something for the Air Ambulance, they were fantastic,” he said.



“I’ have done a few challenges for charity in the past, I really enjoy running and I thought why not I’ll give it a go to keep her memory alive, and to let the family know that we’re thinking of them.

“I’ve been running since 2012 and I’m always out four or five times a week, but I do work 12-hour shifts and nights.

“I just want to go out and get as many people as possible involved.”



Lainie’s ex-boyfriend Cameron Cheng, 18, has been charged with murder and the attempted murder of her mum Rhian Stephens, 38, who was also seriously injured in the attack.

A provisional date for his trial is still set to be fixed.

Lainie was tragically declared dead at the scene when emergency crews arrived at the family home.

An inquest gave a provisional cause of death as “multiple sharp force injuries.”

Lainie’s great-grandmother Florence Jones, 78, told how the teen fought for her life after she was attacked in her bedroom.



Her eight-year-old brother hid under his bed after hearing his sister’s screams.

Paying tribute to her daughter, Rhian said: “Lainie Williams was a typical teenager. She loved every single one of her friends. She didn’t have a nasty bone in her body.

“She was the littlest girl with the biggest heart in the world and she was caring, creative, funny.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“She loved her family, she used to come and kiss me every night and wrap her arms around me.

“She was so caring, she loved everybody – she had all the kindness in the world.”

News.title: Fury as spooky ‘effigies’ suddenly appear at roadside in bizarre long-running neighbour row – with kids left terrified
News.content:
SCARE TACTIC Fury as spooky ‘effigies’ suddenly appear at roadside in bizarre long-running neighbour row – with kids left terrified

VILLAGERS have been left furious as spooky “effigies” suddenly appeared on a quiet country lane, leaving children terrified.

Creepy dummies and stuffed figurines have been carefully arranged on the roadside of Court Hill in Littlebourne, near Canterbury following a long-running neighbour row.



Villagers have been baffled by who is responsible for the bizarre display, prompting complaints about it scaring kids and distracting motorists.

Along with stuffed old fancy-dress costumes, skeletons, and homemade signs, there are several more hanging from a metal gate near a caravan.



Some of the characters are standing up, while others sit down on the grass, wearing unsettling masks with creepy smiles.

One enormous orange creature holds a handwritten sign reading “Dumped here” and “Aspbestos”.



There is also an old-fashioned pram that has a dummy dressed in black and a top hat, hanging on to one side.

The creepy homemade dummies appeared as part of a dispute between a woman living in a caravan and an agricultural business.



Stevie Lowe moved on to land owned by EH Holdstock & Son two years ago – but the business says she did so without permission.

Despite being issued with “official notices”, Stevie has refused to leave the site and has started filling the area with the strange effigies.

Stevie says the display is intended to draw attention to a long-running disagreement over material found near the site which she claims contains asbestos.

It’s not been established what the material is or who originally left it there.

Stevie said: “I informed the farmer and asked him to move it.”



Despite the attention they have attracted, Stevie says the collection is far from finished.

“I’ve got four more effigies to put up,” she said.

Her partner, Dereck Owens, said: “We found the asbestos two years ago in August, so it could have been here for any amount of time before that.”

Stevie says she has refused to leave while it remains there, arguing she is concerned for relatives and other families living nearby.

“Move it, and then I’ll move,” she said. “That’s it. Simple.”



But EH Holdstock & Son strongly disputes her account, saying: “They have never been given permission to be there.

“The correct procedures have been followed and they have been issued numerous official notices to leave in the presence of the police.

“The farm is working with the police, city council, parish council and the courts in addressing the matter.”

The company also alleges the pair have moved asbestos around the land, restricted access, verbally abused staff and vandalised farm equipment.

Stevie admitted she did not ask for permission to move onto the land, but claimed she had previously been told she could stay and strongly denies vandalising equipment or abusing staff.



However, she confirmed she had moved the material she believes is asbestos to the farm’s gates.

Stevie says she was issued with two notices to leave, but claims they did not appear to be from a solicitor.

Meanwhile, the effigies have continued to multiply, with Stevie saying she is aware of complaints about the display and claims she has been told some children find the figures scary.

But she has no plans to take them down while the dispute continues.

Canterbury City Council says there is no active planning enforcement case at the site and that, as it is privately owned, the authority has no involvement in the dispute or rubbish there.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Kent Police also searched its records and said it could find no relevant incidents at Court Hill from the beginning of this year.

A spokesperson said the circumstances appeared to be “more of a civil matter than a policing one currently”.

News.title: Eight rapes in just 20 days on Brit holiday island as hospital is ‘at breaking point’ with tourist-related injuries
News.content:
ISLAND RAPE HELL Eight rapes in just 20 days on Brit holiday island as hospital is ‘at breaking point’ with tourist-related injuries

FEARS are rising for women on an island in Greece after eight rapes were reported in 20 days.

Allegations of sexual abuse have rocked Zante, popular among tourists – particularly Brits – for its vibrant nightlife and stunning beaches.



Michalis Giannakos, president of public healthcare workers’ union POEDIN, said that eight female tourists sought medical attention, reporting that they had been raped.

He said: “It is abhorrent and humiliating what is happening to the women, with individuals taking advantage of the state of intoxication in which they may be.”



Most of the attacks are reportedly linked to the popular area of Laganas.

Police were deployed, and forensic examinations were carried out by the hospital’s gynaecologists.



If you have been affected by the issues raised in the article, please reach out to jeylin.mehmet@news.co.uk

No prosecutions were brought forward as the women reportedly refused to name the alleged perpetrators and did not file charges, as reported by local media.

Giannakos added that a few days ago an Italian tourist needed specialised medical treatment to treat injuries that, according to her, were caused after rape.

A statement from police said: “During the period from May to August 6, three incidents have been reported to our competent service, for which all procedures provided for by law were immediately followed, in cooperation with the prosecutor’s office, forensic and health authorities, and two arrests have been made.”



This comes as two 18-year-old British women have accused a man in Zante of raping them.

Both victims told police they were raped by the same man, according to local media outlet Ethnos.

An urgent probe after the pair were taken to hospital to undergo medical examination.

Upon hearing the horror allegations, the mother of one of the women immediately drove from the UK to Greece.

She managed to track down the suspect to his place of work and attacked him, according to local media.



Officers were called to the scene and the mother and suspect were both taken to the police station.

The suspect has since been arrested on suspicion of rape with a case filed against him.

Authorities are now investigating the complaints and the circumstances around the alleged incidents.

In a separate case, two British sisters were allegedly raped by two UK tourist brothers in Rhodes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Greece has seen sexual violence cases increase sharply over the past 14 years, with police recording 1,250 offences in 2024 compared to just 511 in 2010, according to the latest Eurostat data.



That marks a 145 per cent rise, one of the steeper climbs recorded across the European Union during the same period.

News.title: ‘Brit newlyweds on their honeymoon’ among 3 dead in helicopter crash at Greek holiday island as locals describe horror
News.content:
THREE people including a newlywed Brit couple on their honeymoon have been killed in a horror helicopter crash in Greece, reports say.

The chopper went down on the holiday hotspot island of Sifnos shortly after taking off – with witnesses describing the terrifying aircraft plunge.



The small private helicopter is said to have exploded and gone up in a huge fireball upon impact this evening.

A huge inferno broke out before two firefighters and one fire engine raced to the site to tackle the raging flames, according to local media.



A rescue team from Syros then arrived later on with the Fire Department’s RAFNAR speedboat.

It is currently unclear what caused the helicopter to crash.



It is understood that the pilot was Greek while the two passengers were a British couple.

The pair were reportedly on their honeymoon at the time of the tragedy.



Images shown in local reports showed what appeared to be the crash site on an arid hillside.

Plumes of smoke could be seen billowing from a raging fire near shrubs and bushes.

The chopper, reportedly a Bell 206 helicopter, had just taken off from the island’s helipad in the Tholos area.

The aircraft plunged towards the ground just seconds after taking off, according to the Kathimerini Daily.

It came down and went up in a vicious fireball in an inhabited area – but no homes were hit, it is understood.



The pilot was reportedly hired just two months ago, according to local reports.

One witness told local media that the helicopter began to spin around at a high speed before it smashed into the ground.

Manolis Fountoulakis, deputy mayor of Sifnos, told Greek said: “It experienced mechanical failure in the air, residents say it made a loud, strange noise, like military aircraft.”

The Greek fire service said the crash triggered an alarm heard across the island – a popular tourist destination over the summer season.

News.title: Teens’ college places will be fully funded to help youth inactivity crisis, Ministers say
News.content:
ALL college places will be fully-funded for 16-19 year-olds to help reduce youth inactivity numbers.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell says the cash will be guaranteed for all courses following GCSE results on Thursday.



Teenagers can show up knowing that colleges will be able to afford it in an effort to reduce the one million 16-24 year-olds not earning or learning.

Previously, colleges wouldn’t know if they would get extra funding if more students turned up.



Cabinet Minister Ms Powell said: “Results day was proof of the vital work colleges are doing, delivering lifechanging learning to hundreds of thousands of young people across the country.

“With record numbers receiving T Level results this year, it’s clear demand for high-quality technical education is growing fast.

“But for too long, colleges have only heard warm words from government. I am determined to back them with actions.

“This guarantee means colleges can offer places to every young person who wants one, driving down the number of young people not in education or training, and giving them the skills, experience and confidence to thrive.”

It follows Andy Burnham saying secondary school pupils from aged 14 will be able to study subjects such as AI and manufacturing under major reforms.

He said he was on a “mission” to reduce the number of Neets – those not in education, employment or training – which currently sits at more than one million youngsters.



Labour grandee Alan Milburn is currently conducting a review into the crisis and will publish his report in the autumn.

The PM last month said: “We’ve had a system built for too long around the university route and it sends a message to some young people that they’re some kind of second-class citizens, and it’s just not right.

“They need an education system that works for them as well, that offers a path to all young people, that’s balanced between academic and technical.”

News.title: King Harald V of Norway hospitalised following treatment for blood disorder
News.content:
King Harald V of Norway hospitalised following treatment for blood disorder

King Harald V of Norway has been admitted to hospital following treatment for hemolytic anaemia in recent weeks, the Royal House confirmed

View 2 Images King Harald V of Norway has been hospitalised (Image: Ritzau Scanpix/AFP via Getty Ima)

Europe's oldest monarch has been taken to hospital following treatment for a blood disorder.

‌



King Harald V of Norway has been admitted to the National Hospital, the Royal House confirmed today.

‌



"The King has been treated with cortisone for the blood disease hemolytic anaemia in recent weeks," the statement read. "This has led to fluid accumulation in the body that requires treatment in hospital.

‌



"The King is on sick leave for two weeks. His Royal Highness the Crown Prince is Regent during this period. We will return to the consequences this will have for the Royal House's official program."

Hemolytic anaemia is a blood disorder which occurs when red blood cells are destroyed faster than the bone marrow can make new ones. It can be inherited from parents or acquired later in life due to infections, immune system problems, or certain medicines.

‌



View 2 Images The Royal Palace in Oslo (file) (Image: SplashNews.com)

King Harald, 89, is the oldest reigning monarch in Europe and previously visited the hospital just 10 days ago for a "planned checkup and follow-up with a doctor, and he was driven in his own car".

He was also hospitalised in February, mere days after his birthday, while on holiday with Queen Sonja in Tenerife.

Article continues below

He was treated for an infection and dehydration before returning to Norway.

In 2024 during a visit to Malaysia, he was admitted to hospital after his heartrate dropped dangerously low.

He was fitted with a temporary pacemaker before travelling back to Norway to receive a permanent one.

News.title: Hippo from Pablo Escobar's herd spotted prowling near school as urgent hunt launched
News.content:
Hippo from Pablo Escobar's herd spotted prowling near school as urgent hunt launched

The hippo was spotted walking freely through a quiet neighbourhood in Colombia, with locals watching on as it roamed near a school and approached a home

View 3 Images Shocked residents watched on as the hippo approached a home (Image: Jam Press)

A giant hippo from Pablo Escobar's infamous herd has been spotted roaming near a school, sparking fears for children and alarm amongst residents.

The huge animal was seen wandering freely through a quiet neighbourhood on August 10, with locals watching on as it made its way through the streets and even approached a home.

The shocking sighting unfolded in the El Limonar neighbourhood of Barrancabermeja, Colombia, with one resident filming the hippo as it wandered through the area.

Environment department officials went to the scene to investigate and found tracks showing where the animal had travelled. They believe the hippo entered the neighbourhood through the La Lira creek, apparently emerging from a nearby wetland.

View 3 Images The hippo roamed near a school and approached a home in the El Limonar neighbourhood (Image: Jam Press)

The animal is part of a population that began after notorious drug lord Escobar brought several hippos to his private estate in Colombia in the 1980s. The animals have since multiplied to more than 200 and spread beyond the area where they were originally kept.

Leonardo Granados, the city's Environment Secretary, said a local resident had watched the animal emerge from the area.

He said: "According to the testimony of the young man who was able to observe from this window that the hippo came out, this is where it entered.

"Here are the tracks showing that it flattened all the vegetation, came out, went around that area and then went back in."

The area is now being scoured by vets, biologists and Environmental Police officers in an attempt to locate the animal and establish the route it took.

Authorities are also looking into the possibility it could be the same hippo previously spotted at least three times in rural areas of the municipality.

Granados said the district would work to implement risk-prevention protocols relating to invasive species that could pose a danger to residents. The aim would be to capture the animal and relocate it away from Barrancabermeja.

View 3 Images Pablo Escobar brought several hippos to his private estate in Colombia in the 1980s (Image: Jam Press)

Since January this year, the district has reportedly submitted more than 20 requests to Colombia’s Ministry of Environment and Regional Autonomous Corporations over the presence of hippos in the city.

Several sightings have been reported in Barrancabermeja this year, increasing concerns about the animals venturing into populated areas.

"We are concerned about the safety of children; we are concerned about the safety of families," Granados said. "We are here talking right next to this house; it is already in the urban area."

Authorities have proposed installing camera traps with the Jaguar Foundation to monitor the animal's movements and establish where it is travelling. It remains unclear whether the hippo is the same one seen elsewhere in the department in previous sightings.

Authorities have urged anyone who spots a hippo not to approach it and to immediately report the sighting to the National Police or Environment Department.

News.title: Man found dead outside Asda petrol station in Bradford as police launch probe
News.content:
Man found dead outside Asda petrol station in Bradford as police launch probe

A man in his 40s was found dead after West Yorkshire Police were called to the Asda petrol station on Rooley Lane in Bradford this morning

A man in his 40s has been found dead outside an Asda petrol station.

West Yorkshire Police were called to the Asda petrol station on Rooley Lane in Bradford at around 6.20am today following a report of a concern for welfare.

Officers attended the scene along with ambulance crews, with the petrol station closed to customers while emergency services dealt with the incident, YorkshireLive reports.

Police have now confirmed a man was sadly found dead. His death is currently being treated as unexplained and enquiries are ongoing.

A spokesperson for West Yorkshire Police said: "Emergency services were called to a report of a concern for welfare outside a petrol station on Rooley Lane, Bradford at around 6.20 this morning (17 August).

News.title: Mum of boy, 5, who plunged to death from 15th floor flat says council 'failed' her
News.content:
Mum of boy, 5, who plunged to death from 15th floor flat says council 'failed' her

Five-year-old Aalim Ahmed died after falling from the kitchen window of his family's flat in Plaistow, east London in May 2024

View 3 Images Aalim Ahmed fell from a 15th-floor flat in east London (Image: Getty Images)

A grieving mum has told an inquest her five-year-old son's death was “preventable”, saying he “could have been here” if the council had acted on her safety concerns.

Aalim Ahmed died after falling from the kitchen window of his family's 15th floor home at Jacobs House in Plaistow, east London, on May 16 2024. His father found him on a railing below the block shortly before 6am.

His mother Sahra Osman told Walthamstow Coroner's Court she had repeatedly raised concerns with Newham Council about the safety of the windows before her son's death.

She said Aalim had autism and “no sense of danger”, and believed he may have climbed up while trying to reach a biscuit from a cupboard. Ms Osman claimed the safety restrictors on the windows did not work properly and that repeated visits by workmen failed to resolve the problem.

View 3 Images The incident occurred in May 2024 (Image: PA)

Giving evidence, she became emotional and said: “I did everything I could as a mum to protect my son.” The family had moved into the top-floor property in February 2023, when Ms Osman was heavily pregnant with a daughter. She told the court she had felt “scared” and “horrified” about moving into the flat, which needed repairs, and did not believe it was suitable for her family.

She told the court she had been advised to accept the property and raise her concerns afterwards rather than risk becoming homeless by refusing it.

Ms Osman said she continued raising concerns about the windows after moving in. The court heard she had also informed the council of Aalim's autism diagnosis by email.

She said she believed she had sent a further letter about his condition. People who knew Aalim had also sent a letter to the council saying the family needed to be moved because they were not safe, the inquest heard.

Ms Osman told Sandesh Singh, representing Newham Council: “You guys could have prevented this tragic thing from happening. If you had done your job, he could have been here.

“I think that Newham Council failed me as a mum, as a tenant.

“I tried everything. I tried to tell them my concerns about safety multiple times and you guys ignored me rather than doing anything about the actual issues.”

She added: “I told you my son (Aalim) has autism.

“I do not know what more I can prove. I showed you a GP letter. The people that knew him sent a letter to the council saying this family need to be moved from this flat because they are not safe.”

The inquest heard that an engineer visited the property in January 2024. Ms Osman said she tried the windows during the visit and was still able to open them.

She wanted restrictors fitted to every window and said one bedroom window could be left “just open wide”, which left her feeling “quite scared”.

The engineer said he would look into getting the problem fixed, but Ms Osman said that within a day she found a window restrictor on the floor.

She contacted the council again and said she begged for help and asked to speak to a manager, telling the inquest: “The window was wide open, it would not lock, it was hanging.”

Ms Osman said she made clear that she believed the problem posed a danger to her children, but claimed it was not treated as an emergency. She told the hearing: “The restrictors were not working, they were there for decoration.”

View 3 Images Aalim's father found him on a railing below the block shortly before 6am (Image: PA)

Ms Osman also said she became frustrated as it could take months to receive a proper response from the council. During questioning, the council suggested an engineer had been told about an issue in the living room but not with the kitchen window restrictor.

‌



Ms Osman disputed this and maintained she had raised concerns about windows throughout the property, accusing the council of “not taking my situation seriously enough”.

She also rejected a suggestion that she may have forced a window open during hot weather.

Ms Osman said all the windows were always closed before the family went to bed. On the morning Aalim died, her toddler began shouting “Aalim”, “window” and “outside”, alerting the family that something was wrong.

‌



Ms Osman said her partner went to the kitchen window and was “just crying and screaming in shock” after seeing his son's pyjamas below.

Aalim's father, Makail Ahmed, described the moment as one of “disbelief – it was a nightmare.” He ran downstairs and found his son, while neighbours who had been woken by the noise called 999.

The inquest has previously heard that Aalim was identified by his family and that his cause of death was multiple injuries caused by trauma from a “fall from height”.

Article continues below

Assistant coroner Ian Wade said at the start of proceedings: “One of the things I bear in mind is the horrendous loss borne by Aalim’s family and indeed the community.

“I am very conscious that this should never have happened but how it happened remains to be seen.”

The hearing continues.

News.title: Busted's James Bourne makes first public outing after surgery to 'extend life'
News.content:
Busted's James Bourne makes first public outing after surgery to 'extend life'

Busted star James Bourne, who had to quit the bands tour over his ill health, has been seen out and out amid his mystery illness, just weeks after sharing an update

View 4 Images Busted star James Bourne has made a rare public outing amid his mystery illness (Image: Instagram/disvicious1)

James Bourne has made a rare public outing amid his mystery illness. The singer, 42, who is best known as a member of Busted alongside Matt Willis and Charlie Simpson, had to quit the band's tour with McFly last year and later revealed that he was suffering from poor health.

‌



He has been relatively quiet about his illness and has been seen very little since he made the announcement, but, on Monday, a post on social media which showed him enjoying time with friends.

‌



Guitarist Tommy Henriksen works with Alice Cooper and Johnny Depp's supergroup Hollywood Vampires and a snap appeared on his Instagram Story after the band played in Scarborough over the weekend. A caption on the post read: "My UK friends."

‌



4 View 4 Images James has not publicly disclosed his illness but did say that the underwent surgery to extend his life (Image: Getty Images For Bauer Media) 4 View 4 Images James had to pull out of Busted's tour with McFly last year (Image: Getty Images)

In the photo, James can be seen looking in good spirits, wearing a white T-shirt and a black hoodie slung over his shoulder. James has not disclosed the exact nature of his illness, but did previously say he had undergone surgery to extend his life.

Towards the end of last month, James took to social media to share a rare update, thanking fans for their ongoing support. He wrote: "As I’m taking a break from the gram, I’ll be posting an update soon about what’s going on with my health in my Spotify bio. It’s a long story. Still not out of the woods yet. Thanks for your support and patience."

‌



James issued a statement previously where he said he needed surgery to extend his life. Writing on his Instagram Stories, he wrote: "I realised it's been about six months since I posted last.

View 4 Images Busted shot to fame in the early 2000s and became known for hits like What I Go To School For and Year 3000 (Image: Getty Images)

"I have a plan in place to have a major surgery that should extend my life and hopefully make me well enough to come back to what I love the most, which is touring and making music. It really sucks to be out of the game. But there is hope!"

‌



James shocked his fans when he announced he'd be stepping down from the McFly Vs Busted tour last year owing to his poor health. He said he would miss being there but had to put his health first.

"The VS tour kicks off tomorrow night in Birmingham and as excited as l've been all year for this tour to begin, I'm really sorry to say that over the last 8 days it has become clear that I am not in good enough health to play these shows," he said at the time.

"There's a lot of information I still don't have about my condition but my bandmates, management and I are unanimous in deciding that I should focus on the medical stuff for now.

Article continues below

"I really hope I can be in a position to come back further down the line. It's still going to. be an amazing show and I will miss being there! See you all as soon as possible."

News.title: Sifnos helicopter crash: 'Brit couple on honeymoon' among three killed on Greek island
News.content:
Sifnos helicopter crash: 'Brit couple on honeymoon' among three killed on Greek island

The helicopter went down and sparked a fire in the Tholos neighbourhood on the popular Greek island of Sifnos, with three bodies recovered from the site

View Image Three people have died after a helicopter crashed in Greece

A British couple are reportedly among three people killed in a helicopter crash which sparked a huge fire on the popular Greek tourist island of Sifnos.

‌



The pair are believed to have travelled to the island on their honeymoon and had taken a helicopter ride before it went down shortly after 6pm local time today (4pm UK time).

‌



Rescue crews and firefighters raced to the crash site close to homes in the Tholos neighbourhood and quickly brought the flames under control. The bodies of three people were recovered from the site, the fire department said.

‌



Local news sites report two of the people who died were a British couple honeymooning on the island. The third is said to be an experienced pilot who had worked in the military, and a married dad-of-three.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Four killed in Rio helicopter crash during family trip to celebrate girl's 15th birthday READ MORE :

Utah helicopter crash horror as firefighting chopper goes down tackling wildfire READ MORE :

The helicopter, operated by Bellavia Aviation Services, crashed shortly before it was due to land at Sifnos heliport at around 6:15pm local time.

‌



Emergency services were first alerted to the incident at around 6:10pm, reports Proto Thema.

The crash happened in the Examela area, close to homes and the heliport, the publication reported.

Witnesses claimed they had heard a strange noise as the helicopter approached.

‌



Firefighters attended the scene alongside a rescue team from Syros, which arrived on a high-speed boat operated by the Fire Brigade.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

An image taken in the immediate aftermath showed thick black smoke billowing from a fireball at the crash site.

Article continues below

Sifnos is a stunning island in the western part of the Cyclades island group in Greece, sitting right between Serifos and Milos.

It sits around 76 nautical miles (140 km) from Athens' main port, Piraeus, and is widely celebrated as a culinary hotspot with a rich pottery history and scenic villages.

News.title: Hayden Panettiere dies aged 36: Cause of death update after autopsy
News.content:
Nashville and Heroes star Hayden Panettiere has died at the age of 36, as police launch and investigation and state there was 'no foul play'

US actress Hayden Panettiere, who was best known for her roles in Heroes and Nashville, has died aged 36. Her death was confirmed by her representatives and followed with a statement.

The statement from her father Skip read: “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen.”

The Coroner's office has now confirmed that Hayden's autopsy showed 'no signs of trauma' at the time of her death. It had been reported that the police were responding to a call about a suspected "cardiac arrest", with audio from TMZ confirming dispatchers suspected an "overdose".

A preliminary police investigation has confirmed there were no signs of "foul play or suspicious circumstances" when they arrived at her home after a 911 emergency call from an acquaintance of Panettiere's.

Celebrities including Selma Blair, Viola Davis, Rosie O'Donnell, and singer JoJo have all paid tribute to the star as her former co-stars reach out across the globe.

Her final interviews have also uncovered some of her candid recent comments as she discussed giving up custody of her daughter while struggling with postpartum depression and addiction.

News.title: GCSE results day 2026: What are GCSE grade boundaries and how are they decided?
News.content:
GCSE results day 2026: What are GCSE grade boundaries and how are they decided?

The wait is almost over for the millions of pupils awaiting their GCSE results on August 20 - here's everything you need to know about this year's grade boundaries

View 3 Images GCSE results will be released on August 20 (stock) (Image: Stuart Boulton/Teesside Live)

With GCSE results day around the corner, millions of pupils across England, Wales and Northern Ireland are preparing to find out how they fared in this summer's exams.

‌



Grades will be released on Thursday, marking the end of months of revision, exams and, for many, plenty of nerves.

‌



But while the results are just days away, many will be wondering exactly where this year's grade boundaries fall.

‌



GCSE grade boundaries are not fixed from one year to the next, with exam boards deciding where they should fall once marking is almost complete.

The system is designed to prevent pupils being unfairly penalised if they happen to sit a particularly challenging paper. It means a harder exam can have lower grade boundaries, while an easier exam can result in higher boundaries.

Six ways to use AI to help with GCSE and A Level revision READ MORE :

What are GCSE grade boundaries?

A grade boundary is simply the minimum number of marks needed to achieve a particular grade.

‌



They typically change each year to take account of differences in exam difficulty and help ensure results remain consistent and comparable between different groups of pupils.

In England, GCSEs are graded from 9 to 1, with 9 being the highest grade (sitting above the old A* as a 'super grade'). A U means a qualification is "ungraded".

View 3 Images GCSE grade boundaries differ each year (stock) (Image: PA)

‌



Grade 4 is considered a "standard pass" (equivalent to a low grade C on the former letter-based grading system), while grade 5 or above is considered a "strong pass".

Students who receive a grade 3 or below in GCSE maths or English language will generally have to continue studying the subject and resit the qualification.

The grading system differs elsewhere in the UK. Wales continues to use grades from A to G*, while Northern Ireland also uses letter grades, including the C* grade introduced in 2019.

‌



How are GCSE grade boundaries decided?

Senior examiners will consider the difficulty of each paper, candidates' performance and the quality of the answer before setting the grade boundaries.

This means grade boundaries are determined once exams have been taken and marking is nearing completion.

If a 2026 paper proves harder than its equivalent in 2025, fewer marks could be needed to secure the same grade. If it's easier, the boundary could be higher.

‌



There is therefore no confirmed answer before results day as to whether this year's boundaries are higher or lower than last year's.

Can GCSE marks be rounded up?

It's natural to wonder whether being a mark or two below a boundary could still get you over the line.

Marks are not usually rounded up simply because a candidate falls just short of the next grade.

‌



Pupils should receive marks for individual exam papers alongside their grades, while exam boards publish the official boundaries on results day.

This allows them to see exactly how their marks compare with the threshold.

View 3 Images Official grade boundaries will be published on Thursday (stock) (Image: Nick Wilkinson/Birmingham Live)

Article continues below

There are some cases where marks can be scaled to ensure different parts of the qualification have the correct weighting, with the resulting figures rounded to the nearest whole number.

Modern foreign languages are one example, as listening, reading, speaking and writing are equally weighted - even when components have different maximum raw marks.

Official grade boundaries will be published by exam boards including AQA, Pearson Edexcel, OCR, CCEA and WJEC on results day.

News.title: Lamour leaves Fifa after Infantino plan criticism
News.content:
Fifa's chief operating officer Kevin Lamour has left the governing body less than three weeks after he strongly criticised its president Gianni Infantino's aborted plan to sell stakes in competitions to private investors.

In a statement, a spokesperson said: "Fifa can confirm that the working relationship between Fifa and Kevin Lamour as Chief Operating Officer has ended on 17 August 2026.

"Fifa thanks Kevin for his two years of service and wishes him the best of luck for the future."

It declined to comment on reports that Lamour had been dismissed.

BBC Sport has been told that Fifa's staff were informed of Lamour's departure in an email by its secretary general Mattias Grafstrom on Monday evening.

Last month, Lamour described the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) plans as "the project of one person", and said "the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions".

He added Fifa's own administration was "deceived" about the now abandoned project.

"Our mission - the mission of the hundreds of passionate, dedicated, and exemplary Fifa employees - is to serve football", he added.

"A president must bring people together, unite them, and inspire them. Today, we are experiencing the opposite."

Lamour acknowledged he had a duty of loyalty to his employer but also to "certain values" and supporting his colleagues.

"If that means I lose my job, then so be it," he added. "I will understand and respect that decision. At least I'll sleep well tonight."

Lamour joined Fifa in November 2024, having previously served as deputy general secretary at Uefa, and was two layers of management below Infantino.

Earlier this month, Infantino received the backing of senior executives in a meeting in Morocco, but BBC Sport was told Lamour was not invited.

Lamour has been approached for comment.

In a letter sent to members of Fifa's Council, and seen by BBC Sport, Grafstrom wrote: "I would like to provide you with an important update regarding a change within the Fifa Administration.

"Following recent discussions, Fifa and our Chief Operating Officer, Kevin Lamour have agreed to part ways. This decision was made after careful consideration and with great respect for Kevin, both personally and professionallyâ¦ I felt it was important that I personally provide you this update and I would like to express my gratitude to Kevin for these contributions and for his work and commitment on behalf of Fifa on a daily basis. I wish Kevin all the best for the future."

News.title: Burnham exchanged messages with person posing as Trump's chief of staff
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham exchanged messages with a person posing as the chief of staff to US President Donald Trump.

Downing Street has declined to comment on the security breach, first reported by Politico.

The news website reported that officials said Burnham communicated with the person claiming to be Susie Wiles "before becoming suspicious that the contact was illegitimate" and claimed only a "few messages" were exchanged.

A government spokesperson said: "We do not comment on national security matters."

It is understood the communication between Burnham and the person posing as Wiles was in the form of messages and there was no conversation between the two.

"No messages of significance" were exchanged and the texts were "quickly reported to the appropriate authorities" once they were believed to be suspicious, sources said.

Downing Street did not say when the messages were exchanged, or how many there were, nor whether they were over WhatsApp or another system.

A White House official told the BBC on Monday that the latest incident "had nothing to do" with Wiles' phone being hacked.

The BBC has previously reported an FBI probe into Wiles' phone being hacked in May last year.

At that time, Wiles said her phone had been hacked after an impersonator, or impersonators, used her contacts file to message other top US officials.

The impersonation was targeted at her personal phone, not a government one, but recipients included US senators, governors and top business executives.

Wiles, a key Trump ally, was also among those targeted by a cyber espionage unit associated with Iran's Revolutionary Guards - a powerful branch of Iran's armed forces - in 2024.

Separately, the UK government is in the process of removing the personal mobile numbers of three cabinet ministers from websites where they had been published.

The numbers of Defence Secretary Wes Streeting, Justice Secretary Alex Norris and Northern Ireland Secretary Chris Bryant had all been publicly available online.

A government spokesperson said it had "robust procedures in place to ensure the security of sensitive information".

News.title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told
News.content:
In March last year, the CMS said it would apply for a liability order for Katy's ex, but warned it would take 26 weeks to go to court. Katy was relieved and put a note on the calendar.

But as the date approached, the CMS told her it had still not obtained the order. In September, the CMS again told her it would apply for a liability order - worth about Â£6,000.

Katy said the service told her last month it was no longer confident of her ex-partner's address it needed to send him the paperwork.

She is now in debt herself and her case is, in effect, on hold.

"I was really upset because it just came as such a shock. I thought that I was going to get somewhere and just haven't," she told us.

"I'm not sure I'm ever going to see the money."

Katy's ex-partner did not respond to our questions.

The CMS said it had apologised for delays in progressing the liability order and made a consolatory payment. It said the case has been affected by ongoing difficulty confirming and maintaining a reliable address for the paying parent.

Mother Susan told Panorama the CMS's efforts to chase her ex partner for money owed had been "a waste of everybody's time... a waste of everyone's money".

Her ex stopped paying child maintenance regularly five years ago, and is more than Â£10,000 in arrears. He was abusive, so we have changed her name to protect her identity.

The lack of financial support, she said, meant she had been forced to skip meals.

"No matter how many hours I was working, it wasn't making up for the payments that should have been coming from the paying parent," she said.

In Susan's case, financial investigators at the CMS found her ex had the money to pay. The CMS took him to court but he failed to appear.

The CMS told Susan the court had issued a warrant but it could not take further action.

"They... told me they had no warrant officers," she said, calling it an "embarrassment".

The CMS said it had apologised for failings in this case. It said enforcement action could be complex and it must follow statutory processes.

The DWP told Panorama "continued modernisation" of the service meant it was "progressing cases more quickly and effectively".

Director of the CMS, Simon Hunter, said a lot of the service's 800,000 cases were "highly satisfied" with the service and compliance had improved in the past three years.

"We are working hard behind the scenes to try and make sure that we can facilitate regular child maintenance payments," he said. "Where the case might be in an enforcement which is a very, very small percentage of our customer base, that journey can be quite an extensive period for customers to be in, and I can totally accept and appreciate that it can feel like it has taken a long time."

News.title: Emotional farewell to 'global, iconic superstar' Bonnie Tyler
News.content:
Fans travelled to Wales to pay an emotional tribute to legendary singer Bonnie Tyler as her funeral was held in the city she was "a fantastic ambassador for".

A celebration of life service was held at Swansea Minster ahead of a private family funeral in the village where she was born and grew up.

The Total Eclipse Of The Heart star, whose real name was Gaynor Hopkins, died unexpectedly on 8 July at the age of 75.

Tyler was "one of a kind" and "loved by millions worldwide", talent scout Roger Bell, who discovered her, told mourners at the service in Swansea, while fans shouted "we love you Bonnie" as the cortege left to go to Skewen, Neath Port Talbot.

Bell referenced the tributes, flowers, and cards from the Houses of Parliament, the Prince and Princess of Wales, the Portuguese government, musicians Sir Cliff Richard, Sir Rod Stewart and Suzi Quatro and many fans.

"But in Swansea, she was loved by Robert and the family as Gaynor and auntie Gaynor," he said.

"There was a warmth and sincerity about her that shone through, and she never said no to having a photo taken or giving an autograph to anyone who asked."

News.title: Does Reform's plan to cut £50bn in welfare spending add up?
News.content:
Another big element of Reform's planned cuts comes from taking away benefits from foreign nationals. It claims around Â£20bn could be saved from its Â£50bn target if they were banned from getting benefits including Universal Credit (UC).

More than a million UC claimants were born overseas including around 700,000 EU citizens who arrived in the UK before Brexit and have the right to live and work in the country.

It's important to bear in mind that around half of EU citizens claiming UC are in employment.

The government doesn't provide figures for the number of foreign nationals claiming other benefits.

But taking away these benefit rights would not be a simple thing to do because it risks putting the UK on a collision course with the EU.

Around 4.5 million EU citizens have long-term settlement rights in the UK which means they are eligible to claim benefits.

An estimated one million UK citizens living in the EU have similar rights. Stripping EU citizens of their rights could lead to member states retaliating against the UK.

Reform says it would renegotiate the post-Brexit deal that underpins these rights but that would mean re-opening a process that was supposed to have been settled in 2020.

Another wrinkle in Reform's plan is that its planned savings could disappear if a large number of EU nationals apply to become UK citizens and were able to keep their entitlement to benefits.

News.title: Rain on way for UK with temperatures to drop to overnight lows of 3C in some places
News.content:
High pressure has been dominant this summer leading to hot and dry weather, particularly across England and Wales.

There's been no significant rain in southern England for around two months which has led water levels in our rivers and reservoirs to drop significantly. All of Wales and most of England are in drought.

However, through this week high pressure will be replaced by the influence of low pressure and more unsettled conditions.

Some light rain is likely on Monday, mostly across northern areas of the UK.

Into Tuesday and Wednesday this will turn heavier and start to move into southern England.

While rain is therefore finally going to fall across the south, it may become more showery. This means the exact location and distribution of rainfall is still uncertain.

And while of course any rain will be welcome, it won't bring much improvement to conditions.

It will take weeks of above average rainfall into the autumn to make any significant changes to the drought.

However, it is likely to make a big difference to the emergency services who have been battling against the extreme weather and wildfires over the last few weeks.

The fire severity index - how severe a fire could be, should one start - will come down to low or moderate, according to forecasts from Natural England and the Met Office.

News.title: Princess Eugenie announces name of baby daughter
News.content:
Princess Eugenie has named her baby daughter Adelaide Elizabeth Annina Brooksbank.

Announcing the news on Instagram, she said it was chosen in tribute to "three people we love and admire past and present", including Queen Elizabeth II, and reflected English and Portuguese history - "two places we love and call home".

Adelaide was born earlier this month at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal, weighing 6lb 9oz.

She is Eugenie's third child with her husband, Jack Brooksbank, after their sons August Philip Hawke Brooksbank, born in 2021, and Ernest George Ronnie Brooksbank, born in 2023.

Sharing new photographs of Adelaide, including one of her sons holding their baby sister, Eugenie, 36, wrote: "Two weeks ago today we welcomed our girl to the world. And since then we've had the most special, cosy and love-filled time.

"We are so happy to share Adelaide Elizabeth Annina Brooksbank.

"Named after three people we love and admire past and present, including her great-grandmother who we hold close in our hearts.

"Her name is part of English and Portuguese history, two places we love and call home.

"Augie and Ernie are already the best big brothers."

The name Adelaide is said to have been inspired by Queen Adelaide (1792-1849), who was married to King William IV, as well as Santa Maria Adelaide of Portugal, according to PA Media.

The inspiration for Annina is less clear, but it is believed to be a personal connection to Princess Eugenie and Jack which has not been made public.

The new arrival, who is not a Royal Highness, becomes 15th in line to the throne, moving ahead of her great-uncle, the Duke of Edinburgh, Prince Edward.

A statement from Buckingham Palace at the time of her birth read: "Their Majesties The King and Queen and other members of The Royal Family were delighted to be informed of the news."

Eugenie and her family live between Portugal and Ivy Cottage, in the grounds of Kensington Palace.

Last May, they announced her pregnancy with a photograph of her young sons holding a baby scan with the caption: "Baby Brooksbank due 2026!"

News.title: Boy, seven, among four injured after crash in Ireland that killed five teenagers
News.content:
A seven-year-old boy is among four seriously injured people in hospital after a crash in County Kildare in which five teenagers were killed while driving the wrong way down a motorway.

Two women are in a critical condition, while another woman and the boy are in a serious condition after the head-on crash.

It's believed the injured family - two women aged in their 30s and one in her 20s, and the young boy - were travelling to the airport to go on holiday.

The five teenagers have been named locally as Joe Carthy from Athy, County Kildare, Alex McCarthy from Carlow, Kamil Pustkowski from Limerick, Jeremy O'Brien and Jack Kennedy, according to Irish broadcaster RTÃ News.

Taoiseach (Irish Prime Minister) MicheÃ¡l Martin said his thoughts and prayers were with the injured and the death of the five teenage boys brought untold grief.

News.title: Wildfire phone alert was 'entirely appropriate', government says
News.content:
The government has defended its decision to send an emergency phone alert warning of wildfires across England and Wales last week as "entirely appropriate".

Millions of mobile phones bleeped with a "severe alert" notification on Friday, stating there was a "very high risk of wildfires nationally".

The lack of advance warning for the alert was criticised by charities and domestic abuse survivors, who said there was little chance to protect those hiding secret phones.

The prime minister's official spokesperson said on Monday the first duty of government was to "keep people safe" and the alert had been sent "after a direct request from fire and rescue services on the front line".

They added that at the time of the alert there were 43 fires and 11 major incidents which "stretched resources to the very limit" and required military support.

Most people started to receive the alert from 19:00 BST on Friday, with a message cautioning against the use of disposable barbeques, naked flames or fireworks.

The notification was the biggest use yet of the emergency alert system and Prime Minister Andy Burnham urged the public to take it "seriously".

News.title: Labour MP suspended as party launches investigation into Covid loans
News.content:
A Labour MP has been suspended from the party after a newspaper report questioned whether he had tried to avoid repaying a government Covid loan.

Bayo Alaba referred himself to the Labour Party over the issue and an internal investigation has been launched.

The MP for Southend East and Rochford has also had the whip suspended - meaning he will now sit as an independent MP - although it is understood the investigation does not at this stage imply any wrongdoing.

A Labour Party spokesperson said: "Bayo Alaba MP has referred himself to the Labour Party so that these matters can be investigated in line with the party's rules."

It continued: "The Labour Party expects the highest standards from our elected representatives and we have robust processes in place to ensure those high standards are upheld.

"We cannot comment further while the investigation is ongoing."

The Times newspaper has reported, external allegations that Alaba attempted to wind up one of his business before settling one of two bounce back loans he had taken out.

During the pandemic, taxpayer-funded loans of between Â£2,000 and Â£50,000 were given to small and medium-sized businesses to ease financial problems.

Alaba has admitted taking out two bounce back loans but he insisted he has not tried to avoid his financial obligations and it is understood he believes they will be repaid in full by the end of this year.

Alaba is the registered co-owner of a company called Alaba Properties. Records in Companies House show an attempt was made to wind up the company in March 2022, however, this was blocked for unstated reasons.

A second attempt was then made, which was also blocked in August 2022.

Alaba said: "Like many businesses and entrepreneurs, I accessed financial support during the Covid-19 pandemic.

"I am proud of my background as a small business owner, and of the work I have done since entering politics to support the business community, in part because I know just how difficult things can be.

"There has been no attempt to avoid my financial obligations, and I am wholeheartedly committed to ensuring that the liability is met in full.

"I've referred myself to the Labour Party's investigations process on the matter and I'll cooperate fully."

Mike Wood, a Conservative shadow Cabinet Office minister, said: "These are concerning revelations and Alaba clearly has questions to answer.

"Alaba needs to come clean about whether he tried to avoid paying his debts, and ministers should tell us if they had to intervene to stop it."

News.title: Viral vodka brand Au set to sell for £500m to BuzzBallz owner
News.content:
The viral Welsh vodka firm Au Vodka is nearing a Â£500m sale to Southern Comfort and BuzzBallz owner Sazerac.

Sazerac told BBC Wales in a statement it had agreed to buy the vodka start-up, with the deal, first reported by Sky News, expected to earn Swansea-based founders Charlie Morgan and Jackson Quinn over Â£100m each.

Former Swansea City ball boy Charlie Morgan, who hit the headlines in 2013 after he was kicked by Chelsea's Eden Hazard during a cup semi-final, and his childhood friend Jackson Quinn founded the company in 2015.

The founders declined to discuss the deal, while the owner of the canned cocktail BuzzBallz, Sazerac, said it would allow it "to deepen its presence in the UK".

Two years after launching the vodka firm, Morgan and Quinn accepted investment from DJ Charlie Sloth whose celebrity contacts brought valuable endorsements to the gold-coloured vodka bottles.

YouTube star Jake Paul had a tattoo of an Au Vodka bottle as part of a publicity stunt, while the gold bottles became a staple of poolside parties in Ibiza and Dubai.

The company developed ready-to-drink cans that kept the distinctive gold branding and became one of the most popular products on the market.

In 2025 they opened a new headquarters on an industrial estate in their home city of Swansea, turning an office block into a car park full of gold-wrapped cars, while visitors enjoyed a nine-hole mini golf course with golden obstacles and balls.

News.title: 'Britain's most bashed' bridge hit twice in two days
News.content:
A railway bridge named as the most bashed in Britain has been struck by a lorry for the second time in two days.

Leicestershire Police said that at 05:52 BST on Sunday, the A5 Watling Street near Hinckley in Leicestershire was closed after a lorry crashed into the bridge.

Then on Monday afternoon, the force said the same road was shut due to a "road traffic collision" with a bridge, and officers asked people to find alternative routes.

A Network Rail spokesperson said no damage to the structure was found, but added "bridge strikes remain one of the biggest causes of disruption on the railway".

News.title: Cambridge chancellor criticises 'racist feeding frenzy' around Jason Arday
News.content:
Downing Street declined to say "at this stage" whether Andy Burnham was considering an inquiry into Arday's death, reiterating that it was "a moment for reflection", and that it was right for "the usual processes" like an inquest, to conclude.

An investigation will be carried out to determine Arday's cause of death, which could take several weeks, the London Inner South Coroner's Court has said.

Once complete, and following any submissions from Arday's family, the coroner will confirm if an inquest will take place.

Sir James Cleverly said he was angry about what happened to Arday, and the university establishment - not just Cambridge - should have âdone the robust due diligence and checking that should happen with any senior academic appointment".

Speaking to the BBC's Today programme on Monday, the shadow housing secretary said he felt Arday was used as "bragging rights by some universities", and that people spoke of his "age and his ethnicity rather than his talent".

"I think it was part of the reason that he was lifted so high so quickly and then when the scrutiny did come - external to the universities - his reputation had so far to fall. I think it was unfair on him and I think it's been a terrible, terrible situation."

Sir James - who was Britain's first black home secretary and foreign secretary - said much of the coverage surrounding Arday was "quite possibly" motivated by racism, but that the questions over plagiarism were legitimate, regardless of motivation.

Meanwhile, when housing minister Matthew Pennycook, was questioned over whether the press behaved poorly, he echoed comments by the prime minister that it was not the time to "rush to judgement on this".

"I do think the events leading up to his death raised questions about duty of care and the nature of modern media scrutiny, but I don't think the time is now to get into a debate about those, I certainly don't intend to sit here and opine on them myself," he said.

Pennycook added that it was a time to reflect and "think compassionately about how we got to this situation, which is a desperately, desperately sad one".

The chair of the NHS Confederation, who signed the letter calling for a public inquiry, said focus should be turned on the press, rather than social media, because "self regulation totally failed" in the case of Arday.

Lord Victor Adebowale told the BBC's Radio 4 World At One programme: "People were warned in advance this pursuit risked his life and the warnings were ignored.

"It is true we live in a world of social media where people say what they like and can pursue people as much as they want. In this case I'm pointing at the press. They failed."

News.title: Stag put down after attacking man in Richmond Park
News.content:
A man in his 60s suffered chest injuries after being attacked by a stag in Richmond Park on Saturday.

Royal Parks said the male deer had approached the man's picnic group looking for food, and had since been put down.

Emergency services were called to the south-west London park at 18:16 BST following reports of a deer attack. The Met said a man was taken to hospital, where his injuries were assessed as neither life-threatening nor life-changing.

The charity which maintains London's Royal parks has issued a warning to stay 164 ft (50m) away from the animals following what they said was a rise in visitors feeding wild animals.

A Royal Parks spokesperson said: "We understand from the police that thankfully the injuries were not life-threatening.

"Sadly, the stag's behaviour meant that it had to be put down as it was deemed to be a danger to visitors."

News.title: Reform proposes ban on most benefits for foreign nationals in UK
News.content:
Foreign nationals would be excluded from most benefits under a Reform UK government, the party has said.

The ban, part of a proposed overhaul of Britain's benefits system, would include European Union (EU) nationals with settled status in the UK, meaning a renegotiation of the UK's Brexit deal with the EU.

In a speech on Monday, the party's economy spokesman, Robert Jenrick, said: "The British taxpayer is acting as the welfare state for the world. That's unfair, we all know it."

Reform claims the policy would save Â£21bn a year by its fifth year, but Labour insists the "vast majority" of migrants have no access to benefits and the Conservatives have dismissed the plans as "cobbled together".

Jenrick said there had to be a change of approach to "restore fairness" to the welfare system.

He said one-in-six Universal Credit claimants are not a British or Irish citizen and suggested the money should instead be used to "make the lives of British people better".

This year the government expects, external to spend a total of Â£322bn on welfare in Great Britain, or 10.6% of GDP, just over half of which goes to pensioners.

Reform says it has spent six months drawing up a 50-page plan that it claims will save a total of Â£50bn a year.

Jenrick said the proposals also include a "welfare to work" scheme which will require people who have claimed benefits for more than 12 months to provide 20 hours-a-week of work for their community.

This would apply to those deemed fit to work and will be organised by their local council, the MP said.

Those who fail to take part or poorly perform will face sanctions, including potential cuts to their benefits, according to Reform's policy document.

Jenrick said: "They'll work to clean up high streets and parks, to beautify neglected places, to carry out minor repairs to staff libraries and community centres, to perform many other tasks from the list that we've published today."

In an interview with the BBC, Jenrick would not say how many people would lose access to benefits but insisted his party would treat people claiming benefits "with respect and dignity".

"Those who need them, under a Reform government, will continue to receive them but those people who are shirking, who are taking advantage, they will be reassessed and they will be helped back into the workplace.

"That is the right and fair thing to do."

News.title: Mrs Brown's Boys Christmas specials cancelled after star breaks jaw
News.content:
Brendan O'Carroll, the star and creator of TV sitcom Mrs Brown's Boys, has announced that the show's planned Christmas and New Year specials have been cancelled because he needs an operation on a broken jaw.

The actor and writer, 70, said in a statement on Instagram, external on Monday that filming would no longer go ahead so he can have "immediate surgery".

He wrote: "It is with sincere regret I must announce that due to an unexpected medical issue I will have to cancel the recordings of the 2026 Mrs Brown's Boys Christmas and New Year's Specials.

"Following a CT Scan, it was found that I had two fractures in my mandible (jaw) which requires immediate surgery and a few months recovery."

O'Carroll added that he has been "talking with the BBC about getting Mrs. Brown's Boys back on the screen in 2027".

The long-running comedy series, which is filmed at the BBC Scotland studios in Glasgow, arrived on screens in 2011, starring O'Carroll as foul-mouthed Irish matriarch Agnes Brown.

Despite its many critics, the show remains a hit with viewers, winning multiple comedy prizes at the National Television Awards.
